The second review of 1.24.33 (PowerPoint files, EMF pictures, the AI stop rule) -- findings, worst first.
Replay: node tests/fixtures/pptx_review2_1233/replay.js [src]   (210 cases on the 1.24.33 wip source: 174 AGREE, 36 DISAGREE -- 7 high, 12 medium, 17 low)
Each finding: the input, what Lantern did, what it should do, why it matters. Case ids in [brackets].
Run here: jsdom (Lantern's own script), Chromium through Playwright (the page served from the src), python-pptx 1.0.2,
LibreOffice 24.2 (PDF, PNG, its .pptx/.ppt/.odp/EMF), the ISO/IEC 29500 schemas with lxml. Not run: PowerPoint itself,
Google Slides' and Keynote's own exports (a Google-style file and a streamed zip were written here instead), a Visio EMF,
the in-page (wllama) AI, a phone.

==== HIGH ===========================================================================================================

1. The stop rule puts the model's closing sentence into the block, and nothing is questioned
   [ai-prose-after-slides, ai-prose-after-sheet, ai-prose-after-code; ai-code-end-dot (medium)]
   Input: a reply with no END whose server finish is "stop", where the block is followed by a blank line and prose:
     MAKE SLIDES: Changing a tyre / # Changing a tyre / - Park on flat ground / - Loosen the nuts / - Jack it up /
     (blank) / I hope this helps with your talk!
   (the same after a MAKE SHEET table: "Let me know if you need more items."; after a MAKE CODE Arduino program: "This
   blinks the LED once a second."; and a program ending "END." instead of a bare END.)
   Lantern did: closed the block at the end of the reply, so the sentence is IN the block: the slide's body begins
   "<p>I hope this helps with your talk!</p>" (a plain line is a sentence on the slide, put above its points); the
   table gets a row "Let me know if you need more items."; the program's last line is the English sentence (or
   "END."), which does not compile. All built with ok = true and no problem. Before 1.24.33 each was questioned
   ("cut off before END") and the model was asked once more.
   Should: "stop" says the reply ended, not where the block ended. Close the block at its last line that fits the
   block (for code: before the first blank line followed by prose; for slides/sheet/doc: drop trailing lines after a
   blank line that do not have the block's shape), or keep questioning a block followed by prose. The grammar of
   1.24.31/32 does not prevent this: a first reply is not held to a grammar, and kinds without grammarWords allow any
   line.
   Why: small models very often add a sign-off sentence, and forgetting END is exactly what the rule is for. The person
   presents a slide whose first line is the model talking to them, prints a shopping list with a sentence as an item,
   or uploads a "checked" program that will not compile -- and Lantern told them nothing.

2. EMF: a LineTo inside a path starts a new figure, so paths drawn with lines are filled wrong or not at all
   [emf-path-lines, open-emf-path (high); emf-path-curve (medium)]
   Input: emf/e23_path_lines.emf -- BeginPath, MoveTo(150,20), LineTo(280,280), LineTo(20,280), CloseFigure,
   EndPath, FillPath with a red brush (a red triangle); emf/e09_path.emf -- MoveTo, LineTo, PolyBezierTo, LineTo,
   CloseFigure, StrokeAndFillPath (an arch); r17_emf.pptx slide 3 (the triangle in a deck, opened in Slides).
   Lantern did: draws nothing for the triangle (white where it is red); the arch is filled only above a diagonal and its
   bottom edge is not drawn. LibreOffice draws both as the records say (lo_emf.py).
   Cause: EMF_DRAW's case 54 (EMR_LINETO) calls figure(..., cont=false), and figure() starts a new figure in the path
   when cont is false, so each LineTo becomes a figure of its own two points (src line ~50524). In GDI only MoveTo
   starts a figure; LineTo goes on with it (POLYLINETO already passes cont=true).
   Why: MoveTo/LineTo paths are the plainest way a program writes a filled shape (LibreOffice itself writes its curves
   as paths with LineTo, lo_dashes.emf). A Visio or CAD drawing's filled shapes vanish or are cut diagonally, and the
   dialog only says the EMF was "drawn by Lantern".

3. A chart's percent sign written as text multiplies the number by 100
   [read-chart-literal-percent, read-chart-escaped-percent]
   Input: r03 slide 6, values 40 and 65 with number format 0"%"; r15 slide 2, values 92 and 88 with format 0\%
   (Excel's way to show a % after numbers typed as whole percents).
   Lantern did: 4000% and 6500%; 9200% and 8800%.
   Should: 40% and 65%; 92% and 88%. Only a % outside quotes and not escaped scales by 100 (chartTable's shown(): test
   /%/ on the format after taking out "quoted text", \x escapes and [brackets], as the date test already does).
   Why: the table of a chart's numbers is all a person (and a model reading the deck) gets of the chart; numbers wrong
   by a factor of 100 are wrong facts.

==== MEDIUM =========================================================================================================

4. Reading order: grids are read down their columns, a staggered timeline out of order, column headings across
   [read-grid6-low, read-grid4-gutter, read-grid4-uneven, read-timeline-staggered, read-column-headings-close;
   read-timeline-two-rows (low)]
   Input (r13, r02; python-pptx text boxes on Title Only): six numbered steps "1. Isolate" ... "6. Restore" in a 3 by 2
   grid (gaps 0.5 in across, 0.25 in down); four numbered steps for mixing mortar in a 2 by 2 grid with a gutter;
   four seasons in a hand-placed 2 by 2 grid; a timeline of five years above and below its line in turn; a heading over
   each column 0.15 in under the title box.
   Lantern did: 1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 6; 1, 3, 2, 4; Spring, Autumn, Summer, Winter; 1985, 2001, 2020, 1992, 2012; Petrol
   engines, Diesel engines, then all the points. (The same six steps 0.3 in higher, right under the title, come out
   1 to 6 -- read-grid6-tight agrees -- because the slide's own title takes part in the cut and its gap decides.)
   Should: a grid of like boxes is read row by row (as its numbers say); a timeline left to right; a heading with its
   column. Two changes would do most of it: cut without the title box (it is the slide's h already); and prefer rows
   when the boxes form a grid (each row's boxes share their tops and sizes) -- the column rule is for a heading or a
   column of different boxes. A timeline whose boxes overlap across but not down is one line, read left to right.
   Why: a lockout or a mortar recipe read 1, 4, 2, 5 on the slide (and to the model) is a procedure out of order.

5. The stop rule misses a whole short block when Lantern changed the reply's start
   [ai-think-short, ai-read-head-short]
   Input: "<think>...</think>" then a three-point deck (under 200 characters), finish "stop"; and "= MAKE SLIDES:
   Tyre" (the = of a formula line, as the 0.8B and 2B write it, read by AI_READ as MAKE SLIDES) with two points, "stop".
   Lantern did: "the deck was cut off before END" -- the rule compares the last 200 characters of the server's reply with
   the last 200 of the text Chat builds; for a reply shorter than 200 those include its start, which clean() (think) or
   AI_READ changed.
   Should: compare the text with what Lantern made of the last reply (AI.lastRaw / the cleaned, read text), or compare
   only as many characters as the shorter of the two.
   Why: short blocks from small models are the rule's main case (an oil change of three steps).

6. Saved text in capitals is not shrunk and runs off the slide in PowerPoint
   [write-fit-capitals]
   Input: a slide of six safety-sign bullets in capitals ("DANGER: HIGH VOLTAGE - KEEP OUT UNLESS AUTHORISED AND
   ISOLATED", 60 to 70 letters each), saved as .pptx.
   Lantern did: stored it at 100% (no fontScale). Laid out with Georgia's widths (Gelasio, check_fit.py) it needs 396 pt
   in a 335 pt box (374 pt even at 1.14 line height): the last line runs past the slide's bottom until someone edits it.
   Mixed-case text fits (write-fit-twelve, -long-title, -beside-picture agree).
   Should: count capitals wider than half an em (Georgia's capitals are about 0.56 em to 0.7 em, lowercase about 0.44).
   Why: warning and safety slides are the ones written in capitals.

7. A chart with two levels of categories names rows by the outer level
   [read-chart-two-levels]
   Input: r15 slide 1, Q1 and Q2 under 2023 and 2024 (c:multiLvlStrRef).
   Lantern did: rows named 2023, Q2, 2024, Q2 (the outer level's points, at the first index of each group, overwrite
   the quarters).
   Should: Q1, Q2, Q1, Q2 with their year ("2023 Q1", ...): read the first c:lvl (the leaves) and add the outer label.

8. SmartArt steps in the order of the list of points, not of the diagram
   [read-smartart-order]  (unsure whether PowerPoint writes points out of order; the spec gives sibling order by srcOrd)
   Input: r14, a process whose fourth point "Tag" is last in ptLst but third by its connection's srcOrd.
   Lantern did: Isolate, Lock, Prove dead, Tag.  Should: Isolate, Lock, Tag, Prove dead (siblings by srcOrd).

==== LOW ============================================================================================================

9. A block ended by the next block is still "cut off before END" [ai-two-blocks-first-open]
   "MAKE DOC: ... (no END)" then "MAKE SLIDES: ... END", finish "stop": the DOC is questioned as cut off, though the
   model went on to the next block (as before 1.24.33; the rule closes only the last block).

10. Right-to-left text is saved left to right [write-rtl]
   <p dir="rtl"> and <li dir="rtl"> (which PPTX_READ makes from rtl="1") are written without rtl="1"; LibreOffice sets
   the Arabic from the left, and Lantern reads it back without dir. Round trip loses it.

11. LibreOffice numbers a second list on from the first [write-num-restart-shown]
   "Morning: 1. 2.  Evening: 1. 2." saved and opened in LibreOffice shows Evening 3. 4. (PowerPoint restarts after a
   paragraph with no number, I believe; LibreOffice goes on). Writing startAt="1" on a list's first item would tell
   both. Lantern's offline users are the ones likely to open the file in LibreOffice.

12. Text after a table is saved above it [write-text-after-table]
   "<p>The rota for the week:</p><table>...</table><p>Swap with a friend if you must.</p>": both lines go in the
   content box above the table; read back, the last line comes before the table.

13. Chart dates and decimals not as the chart shows them
   [read-chart-percent-decimal, read-chart-day-dates, read-chart-years, read-chart-us-dates]
   0.0% shows 91.25% (chart 91.3%); d-mmm-yy shows "Mar 2025 3" (chart 3-Mar-25 -- the day after the year reads as
   odd); yyyy shows 2022-01-01 (chart 2022); m/d/yyyy shows 2025-03-04 (chart 3/4/2025; ISO is unambiguous, unsure
   which a person wants).

14. A damaged [Content_Types].xml: "this zip file has no PowerPoint presentation in it" [damaged-content-types]
   The presentation and every part are there (ppt/presentation.xml, the package relationships); PowerPoint offers to
   repair. Lantern refuses with a sentence that is not true; reading it (the parts are found by relationships) or saying
   "damaged" would be right.

15. Open .pptx leaves a file box on the page when the chooser is closed with no file [open-chooser-closed]
   In SLIDES_PPTX the line `inp.style.display = "none";` sits after `// a show and a template too (the first review)`
   on the same line, inside the comment (src ~51738), so the input is shown; when no file is chosen no change event
   comes and it stays at the bottom of the page (366 by 40 px). Slides' own Insert picture hides its input and removes
   it after 2 s.

16. EMF: parts drawn otherwise than Windows draws them (said as "parts Lantern does not draw yet" where not drawn)
   [emf-hatch, emf-gradient, emf-pie, emf-xor-twice, emf-dib-sharp, emf-lo-image]
   - a hatched brush (BS_HATCHED) fills solid: a black block where Windows draws thin crossed lines (LibreOffice 24.2
     also fills solid);
   - EMR_GRADIENTFILL and EMR_PIE are not drawn; a picture of only those gives nothing (LibreOffice draws the pie, not
     the gradient);
   - R2_XORPEN drawn as "difference": the same red box twice leaves grey (185,195,195), not nothing (LibreOffice draws
     red);
   - small bitmaps stretched big are smoothed; Windows' default stretch mode (and SETSTRETCHBLTMODE, which is ignored)
     draws sharp pixels (LibreOffice also smooths).

==== AGREED (the main things that held) ==============================================================================
Title/subtitle, levels, Section Header, Two Content, Comparison, Picture with Caption, notes with pauses, core title;
chevrons, a timeline in a row, a heading over two columns, column headings at the usual distance, a picture beside
words, nested groups; tables with joined cells; charts with 0%, mmm yyyy, several series; looks and links; hidden
slides and sections said; empty title box, no title box, a lone line; every numbering type and start; RTL read; six
photos, crops, turns and flips (put together right in the browser); GIF, BMP, TIFF said; 16:9 and footers; SmartArt
lists; a Google-style file, Strict names, a streamed zip, .pptm/.ppsx/.potx, LibreOffice's saves; every damaged and
wrong file but #14 refused or read with a plain sentence (empty, cut short, text, Keynote, photos zip, Word, Excel,
.ppt -- hand-made and LibreOffice's --, .odp, PDF, locked); markup meant to run a script stays text (in jsdom and in the
page). Saved decks: every part valid against the schemas, every part typed and every relationship's target there,
python-pptx and LibreOffice open them with every title, dark and light themes drawn as chosen (Dark 1 the darker),
numbering types shown by LibreOffice, joined cells, long text and long titles shrunk to fit, pictures beside and
across, links with spaces, notes, odd characters, an empty deck, round trips, MAKE SLIDES' deck, LibreOffice's re-save.
EMF: shapes, polygons, text (also turned), both map modes, LOMETRIC, world transform, save/restore, clips, DIBs of
1, 8 and 24 bits, polypolygon holes, offset frames, dashed pens, EMF+ dual, PATCOPY, isotropic, and LibreOffice's own
EMFs (shapes, text, gradient bands, curves, clip). AI: stop closes a whole block, length/none/null do not, END, trailing
space, a long block after <think>, mid-line stop, whole code with blank lines, two blocks, an older reply after a newer
call, runaway still found, lastReply/lastFinish kept as sent.
